summary: [P1] Keep healthy quiet executions and human approval waits alive
failure_scenario: The watchdog marks every running reply failed after 120 seconds without a conversation event, including a healthy long native tool/provider request and a pending human approval. No new Node/PA execution path emits run_heartbeat, and awaiting_permission_at is ignored. An isolated server reproduction with a shortened watchdog marked both an active quiet-tool message and a freshly pending approval failed. Subsequent message_delta frames are discarded because gateway.ts requires delivery_status=running. Restore execution-specific liveness and approval-wait handling so genuine dead runs still time out without falsely failing healthy work.

summary: [P1] Emit the retained client token-usage schema
failure_scenario: A normal DSH reply is sent to IM with prompt/completion/cache_read/cache_total_input, while the retained Web and Swift clients consume context_used/output/cache_read_tokens/cache_total_input_tokens. IM stores and forwards this object without conversion. Web renders NaN context utilization; expanding TokenChip calls undefined.output.toLocaleString() and throws. An independent execution of the frozen projection produced exactly these renamed keys and the TypeError. Normalize the product payload at this boundary and preserve unknown counters instead of manufacturing zero; cover real message serialization through client consumption.

summary: [P2] Refresh public readiness and runtime PID across supervisor recovery
failure_scenario: lifecycle.ready is written only once during initial startup. RuntimeSupervisor clears only its private ready flag when DSH exits and replaces the process during recovery, so public pa status and persisted state retain ready=true and the dead initial runtime PID. An isolated real-node reproduction killed DSH PID 33272, observed replacement 33287, and still received RUNNING pid=33254 ready=true DSH=33272. Retry exhaustion likewise leaves a connected but non-executable node publicly ready. Publish runtime unavailable/recovered transitions into lifecycle state and refresh the owned runtime PID; verify status through crash, recovery and exhausted retries.
